title: Stochastic magnet latch: random nanomagnet made exact by self-feedback
idea: Random AND deterministic: a 10 nm superparamagnetic MTJ (barrier ~15 kT, flips in ns) drives a 2-transistor loop that sends a small spin-orbit bias current reinforcing whatever state it reads, turning a p-bit into a latch. Residual thermal escapes up to 1% BER are allowed and corrected by a row-level code on read.
why: Magnet needs no thermal stability, so ~3x smaller and ~5x lower write current than MRAM; static while powered; 1% tolerance is what makes the tiny barrier viable.

title: Pinned nanobubble bit: a bubble that should dissolve but persists
idea: Surface nanobubbles pinned at a pore rim are paradoxically stable for hours: electrolysis nucleates an H2/O2 bubble in a sealed 20 nm pore (1) and reverse polarity recombines it on a Pt catalyst rim (0), read by impedance. Stochastic nucleation causes ~1% failed writes, absorbed by a 1%-BER code instead of verify loops.
why: Static bit from water and Pt traces with huge impedance contrast; tolerating stochastic nucleation enables ns-scale writes without verify.

title: Dark-exciton reservoir: light stored without light
idea: Interlayer excitons in a MoSe2/WSe2 moire trap array are charge-neutral but carry a permanent dipole and live us-ms when dark; inject by a gate-pulsed tunnel-electroluminescent junction, read the dipole's capacitive Stark signature, refresh in place. Ensemble loss of ~1% per window is handled by code.
why: Density set by ~8-10 nm moire period with no capacitor; 1% BER tolerance relaxes the lifetime spec that would otherwise kill it.

title: Shelved rare-earth bit: excited ions as a leakage-immune capacitor
idea: Er3+ ions in a 10 nm silicon-rich oxide pocket have a ~10 ms metastable 4I13/2 level; hot-electron impact excitation charges the ensemble with energy, and readout uses energy back-transfer to Si nanocrystals that yields a sensed photocurrent burst. Excited AND stable: energy, not charge, so junction leakage cannot drain it; 1% misses coded away.
why: Retention set by atomic radiative lifetime, immune to the transistor leakage tail (fact 3); non-charge storage at 10 nm.

title: Valley bit: holes parked in K versus K-prime valleys
idea: Resident holes in monolayer WSe2 hold valley polarization for us-ms because spin-valley locking blocks flips; a chiral spin-orbit write pulse populates K or K', read by valley-Hall voltage on a 20 nm cross. Same charge in both states, so no leakage drift; only flips, kept under 1% by refresh plus code.
why: Charge-neutral state variable removes leakage-driven decay (fact 3); ~20 nm 2D cells; 1% tolerance makes us-scale valley lifetimes usable.

title: Negative-U defect ensemble: yield killers held as bits
idea: Bistable DX-type centers (Si in AlGaN, or C_i-C_s pairs in Si) capture an electron pair with large lattice relaxation, so emission needs a ~0.5 eV configurational barrier; a 20 nm channel with ~100 centers is written by carrier injection and read by conductance. Each defect is random, the ensemble digital: Poisson statistics set ~1% cell BER, absorbed by code.
why: Retention from configuration barrier rather than junction isolation (fact 3); capacitor-free; a reliability defect becomes the store.

title: Stacking-fault bit: SiC bipolar degradation reversed into memory
idea: In 4H-SiC, forward current makes partial dislocations glide and expand a single Shockley stacking fault (bipolar degradation); a heat or reverse pulse shrinks it. The bit is fault expanded vs retracted across a 30 nm channel, read as a resistance step; glide is stochastic, giving ~1% misses the controller tolerates.
why: Turns a SiC failure mode into a static capacitor-free element on US-made SiC wafers; 1% tolerance avoids verify cycles.

title: One-way forgetting cell: undersized capacitor plus Z-channel code
idea: Forgetful only in one direction, exact overall: DRAM cells leak 1->0 but almost never 0->1, so shrink Cs to ~1.5 fF (AR ~25:1) and accept 1% 1->0 errors, decoded with an asymmetric Z-channel (Berger-type) code needing about half the redundancy of symmetric ECC.
why: Breaks the capacitor charge wall (fact 1) by cutting AR ~2.5x and removing HAR etch steps; ~6% code overhead vs ~12% symmetric.

title: Hierarchical-modulation cell: robust bit and noisy bit share one capacitor
idea: Store 4 levels as polarity plus amplitude: polarity is the exact data bit, the amplitude LSB is allowed 1% BER and carries parity/soft-check for neighbouring cells, as in broadcast-TV hierarchical modulation. Exact AND sloppy in one charge packet.
why: 1.5-2x information per cell without MLC-grade sensing because only the MSB must be exact; ~+50% density.

title: Unary-coded low-bit weights: 1% flips become 1% numeric noise
idea: Encode 2-3-bit quantized AI weights/activations as thermometer codes in 3-7 tiny cells so any single flip moves the value by one LSB, never a sign/MSB; cells then run at 1% BER with ~4x smaller capacitors and no ECC. Wasteful coding, efficient silicon.
why: ~2.5x net density for AI tensor storage (1.5-2x cells at 1/4 area) and no ECC logic; attacks fact 1 for the dominant AI workload.

title: Pulse-position group: which cell is charged, not how much
idea: Store 3 bits as the position of one charged cell among 8 sub-fF cells sharing a sense node; read is winner-take-all max detection needing no reference and immune to common-mode leakage and temperature. Sub-cells are ~1/6 normal size because 1% BER at max detection is acceptable and coded.
why: Reference-free sensing shrinks sense-amp periphery (fact 7) and capacitor (fact 1); ~2x density vs 3 full-size cells.

title: Retention-reject harvest: failed DRAM dies sold as 1%-BER memory
idea: Bin dies that fail JEDEC retention or show weak-cell clusters into a soft grade, pair them with a controller doing 1%-BER coding plus 4x refresh, and sell them into AI training/inference cache tiers. Defective AND useful: yield loss becomes supply.
why: Raises effective bit supply 5-15% with zero new fab capex; no new materials.

title: Sloppy-overlay DUV arrays: imperfect patterning accepted at 1% BER
idea: Pattern storage-node landing pads with immersion-DUV double patterning at relaxed overlay, accepting ~1% shorted/missing cells; map them at test into an on-die erasure table and code around them instead of using 2-3 EUV layers.
why: Cuts EUV dependence and mask count (fact 4); erasure decoding of known-bad cells costs ~2% overhead.

title: Poly-Si 3D tiers that tolerate the grain-boundary leakage tail
idea: Stack 32+ tiers of lateral deposited poly-Si access transistors with simple planar capacitors; grain boundaries fatten the leakage tail, so refresh for the 99th percentile and let 1% of cells fail, coded per tier. Bad devices, good memory.
why: Makes 3D DRAM (fact 2) viable with cheap poly-Si instead of epitaxial Si/SiGe stacks; ~3-5x density over planar at modest capex.

title: Canary sub-cell per row: a deliberately weaker cell guards the rest
idea: Each row carries two half-size canary capacitors holding known data; when a canary fails the row is scrubbed, and the row otherwise runs at the longest interval where <=1% of data cells fail, with canary flags turning those failures into located erasures.
why: 4-8x longer refresh interval (fact 3) for ~1% area; an intentionally worse cell makes the row exact.

title: 99%-success writes: sub-critical pulses for switching elements
idea: Probabilistic AND reliable: write magnetic or phase-change elements with pulses sized for 99% success instead of 1-1e-9 and skip verify; failed writes appear as 1% BER cleaned by read-side code. Because switching energy scales with ln(1/error), write energy and time fall 2-4x.
why: Energy per bit and write latency (facts 5,10); lets slow-tailed elements reach DRAM-class write speed.

title: Below-the-floor array: run VARY at 0.45 V with 1% errors
idea: Drop array/bitline voltage from ~1 V to 0.45 V with proportionally lower wordline boost, accepting 1% sensing errors from offset and noise, corrected per row. CV^2 array energy falls ~5x.
why: Breaks the voltage floor (fact 10) and cuts refresh energy; no new materials.

title: Hammer-tolerant pitch: let neighbors disturb, then correct
idea: Shrink storage-node and wordline spacing ~20% past row-hammer-safe limits and treat disturbance flips, bounded to 1% by activation-count throttling, as noise corrected by a hammer-aware code that weights recently aggressed rows. Fragile AND dense.
why: ~1.4x density with no new litho; reframes facts 4 and 9 as a BER budget.

title: Mature-node good-enough DRAM: US 28 nm fabs making 1%-BER cells
idea: Policy plus IP: fund an open 1%-BER-tolerant controller standard and a trench-capacitor 1T1C module for idle US 28-40 nm logic fabs, yielding memory ~3x larger per bit than leading DRAM but sold for AI cache tiers where 1% raw BER is coded away. Old node, new memory.
why: US manufacturability and capital intensity: reuses depreciated fabs, adds domestic supply in 18-24 months vs 3-5 years.

title: Weak-cell Bloom filter: known errors are not errors
idea: At test, record each bank's weakest 1% of cells in a compact on-die Bloom filter (~0.1% of bits, no fuses); reads treat flagged cells as erasures, roughly doubling the correction power of the same ECC so cells can run at 1% raw BER.
why: Lets refresh interval stretch ~4x and capacitor shrink ~30% (facts 1,3) for ~0.1% storage overhead.

title: Four forgetful quarters: charge-summed sub-cells dilute the leakage tail
idea: Split each capacitor into four isolated quarter cells with minimal access devices and charge-share all four onto the bitline at read; a leaky-tail quarter (1% chance each) only costs 25% of signal, so the sum stays readable. Four forgetful parts make one faithful whole.
why: Converts the leakage-tail outlier (fact 3) from a bit failure into a 25% signal loss, allowing 4-8x longer refresh; area near-neutral with stacked quarters.
